About

One person,
obsessive about the details.

I'm 17, I'm based in London, and I build websites — properly, one at a time. This isn't something I picked up to earn on the side. It's the thing I've been pulled towards for years, and it's what I spend my hours on when nobody's asking me to.

Most sites at this price come off a template, because templates are quick. I don't work that way. Every project starts as a blank file, and I stay with it until the small things are right — how a headline arrives on screen, how a button answers the cursor, how the whole thing holds up on a four-year-old phone. That takes longer. It's also the entire difference between a website that exists and one people remember.

What I specialise in is 3D. Real WebGL, rendering live in the browser — not a video, not a picture of something 3D. Hardly anyone building for small businesses is doing this yet, and that is exactly the point: every competitor on your high street has a site that looks like every other site on your high street. Yours won't.

Being 17 isn't the caveat — it's the reason. I'm not carrying a decade of habits from an older way of building the web, and I'll give your project the hours a busy studio simply hasn't got.

I'd rather build ten sites people remember than a hundred nobody does.
Founded and run by
17

Privacy policy.

Last updated 4 October 2026

I'm NextMotionDigital, one person building websites in London. This explains what I collect, why, and what you can ask me to do with it. Questions go to anikitouv@gmail.com.

What I collect

  • When you book a call: your name, email, business name, phone number if you give it, your message, and the project type, budget and time you choose.
  • When you become a client: what I need to build your site, such as your text, images and any logins you share for your domain or hosting, plus invoices and payment records.
  • When you visit: I don't track you. Like every website, the services that deliver this page see your IP address. See "Who else is involved" below.

Why I use it

  • To reply to your enquiry and quote you a price. Legal basis: steps you've asked for before a contract.
  • To build and deliver your project. Legal basis: our contract.
  • To keep tax and accounting records. Legal basis: a legal obligation.

I never sell your details, add you to a mailing list or use them for advertising.

How your booking reaches me

Depending on how the form is set up, it either opens your own email app with your details filled in, so nothing is sent until you press send, or it passes them to a form-delivery service that forwards them to my inbox.

Who else is involved

  • Google: my email runs on Gmail, and this page's fonts load from Google Fonts, so Google sees your IP address when the page loads.
  • GitHub: hosts this website and keeps short-term server logs, including IP addresses, for security.
  • Services a project needs: for example hosting, domain or payment providers, which we agree before any are used.

Some of these companies store data outside the UK. When they do, they rely on safeguards recognised under UK data protection law.

How long I keep it

  • Enquiries that don't become a project are deleted within 12 months.
  • Client and payment records are kept for six years, because UK tax rules require it.

Your rights

You can ask for a copy of what I hold about you, ask me to correct or delete it, or object to how I use it. Email me and I'll reply within one month. If you're unhappy with how I've handled your data, you can complain to the Information Commissioner's Office at ico.org.uk.

Project previews

Projects you open from "Sites I've built" are live websites. They load from their own addresses, and their own privacy policies and cookies apply.

Terms & refunds.

Last updated 4 October 2026

The short version
  • No refunds once work has started.
  • 50% deposit to start, 50% when you sign off the finished site.
  • Once it's paid in full, you own the code and the domain.

These terms apply to every website project from NextMotionDigital. Paying the deposit means you agree to them.

Price

Every project gets a fixed price and a delivery date, agreed in writing before I start. The price covers the scope we agree. Anything outside it, like extra pages, new features or a change of direction, is quoted separately, and nothing extra is charged without your agreement.

Payment

  • A 50% deposit is due before work starts. Work begins once it's paid.
  • The remaining 50% is due when you sign off the finished site. Before sign-off, I'll make any changes needed so it matches what we agreed.
  • Outside costs, such as a domain name, are agreed before we start. Nothing is recurring unless you ask for it.

Refunds and cancellation

  • Payments are non-refundable once work has started. Your deposit pays for design and build time that's already been spent.
  • If you cancel before any work has started, I'll refund your deposit in full.
  • If you end a project part-way through, the deposit isn't refunded, and you won't owe the remaining 50%.
  • If something I built doesn't work the way we agreed, tell me and I'll fix it free of charge.

Your legal rights

Nothing in these terms affects your rights under UK law. If you're buying as a private individual rather than for a business, you can cancel within 14 days of agreeing the project. If you ask me to start within those 14 days and then cancel, you pay only for the work done up to that point and I refund the rest. If the site is finished and delivered within those 14 days at your request, the right to cancel ends at that point.

Ownership

Once the project is paid in full, you own the code and the domain. Until then, the work stays mine. I may show the finished site in my portfolio. Just tell me if you'd rather I didn't.

Your content

You're responsible for the text, images and logos you give me, and for having the right to use them.

Liability

I'm not responsible for problems caused by outside services, such as hosting, payment or email providers, or by changes anyone else makes to the site after handover. My total liability for a project is limited to the amount you paid for it, except where the law doesn't allow that.

Law

These terms are governed by the law of England and Wales.
